A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and some reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v5 reports original LLM forgetting measurements, prediction and replay experiments, and Rotated-MNIST simulations, including Table 2, Figure 7, and Appendix F.

after.justification: v6 retains original empirical results and adds prediction, training-setting sensitivity, and replay analyses, including Tables 5–11 and Appendices D, F, H, and I.

M1.justification: The additive, MF, KNN, and targeted-replay procedures remain. Appendix I adds a hybrid predictor that fits matrix-completion residuals with an embedding model. This is a localized method extension rather than a replacement of the central approach.

E1.justification: v6 adds 18 OLMo2-SFT-Mix fine-tuning tasks, including coding, mathematics, and safety-related tasks, to the instruction-model study. Downstream evaluation now follows four held-out tasks from this mixture instead of Dolly. The separate base-OLMo downstream benchmark evaluation in v5 Table 4, including SciQ and Winogrande, disappears. Most original corpora and Rotated-MNIST coverage remain.

E2.justification: The principal external prediction baseline is substantively replaced: v5 uses a trainable OLMo-1B encoder and regression head, whereas v6 uses a frozen sentence transformer with two trainable MLP layers. This is more than renaming Similarity to Embedding. The revised downstream replay comparison also reports MF-Offline instead of KNN-Offline.

E3.justification: The reported OLMo-Instruct budget for MMLU, BBH, and TruthfulQA changes from 37 to 100 steps; OLMo2-SFT-Mix uses 1,000 steps. Dolly replay changes from every 32 to every 8 steps, and Token F1 is added for replay evaluation. New experiments vary MF rank, learning rate, and batch size. These documented changes do not establish which retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v6 adds tests of prediction sensitivity to MF rank (Table 5), whether targeted replay impedes new-task learning (Table 6), learning-rate and batch-size sensitivity (Table 9), replay-induced changes in forgetting patterns (Table 10), and embedding–matrix-completion complementarity (Table 11). These substantially extend the earlier model-size, similarity, and synthetic analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H adds an explicit comparison between two training random seeds as a control. The ten sampled seed-set repetitions, paired t-tests, and domain z-tests were already reported in v5. v6 retains the general single-run statement for collecting forgetting statistics.

E6.justification: Prediction results change: MF's in-domain OLMo-Instruct F1 is 57.35 in v5 Table 2 and 58.16 in v6 Table 3, alongside revised task and training settings. The embedding baseline scores are replaced and LoRA prediction columns disappear. v6 adds substantial sensitivity, new-task learning, Token F1 replay, and hybrid results, while replacing the Dolly-based downstream tables with OLMo2-SFT-Mix results.

T1.justification: The forgetting-matrix definitions, low-rank and logistic factorization objectives, and Taylor-expansion/random-projection arguments are retained. Symbol corrections do not introduce new mathematical reasoning. No new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: low-rank forgetting associations, matrix-completion prediction, and targeted replay that reduces upstream forgetting. Updated illustrative scores and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v6 adds substantive limitations concerning theoretical guarantees, supervised-only training, sampled upstream data, and beneficial versus harmful forgetting, including privacy and outdated-knowledge concerns. New analyses introduce interpretations about learning tradeoffs, batch-size effects, and embedding complementarity. Appendix I's claim of improvement over both component methods is overbroad for Table 11's out-of-domain OLMo-Instruct results.

D1.justification: v6 newly documents GPU hardware, dataset licenses, learning-rate selection using five FLAN tasks, and the all-distilroberta-v1 baseline encoder. Conversely, v5's LoRA adapter rank and 625-step training details are omitted despite retained LoRA results. Most sampling, matrix-completion, and replay implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v6 adds references and limited discussion covering Sentence-BERT, software risk management, unlearning, synthetic rehearsal, and further empirical forgetting studies. Examples include Reimers and Gurevych, Boehm, Nguyen et al., and Zheng et al. The Gao et al. evaluation-framework reference is removed. The central novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: v6 makes numerous local language corrections, rewrites selected baseline and discussion passages, and adds a risk-management analogy. Appendices are reorganized, with limitations first and the impact statement moved to Appendix B. The six-section main narrative and much of its wording remain.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to predominantly one column. Rank/model-size plots are consolidated, component heatmaps are expanded and relocated, replay panels change, and several tables are added. Rotated-MNIST Figures 13–14 become Figure 12, whose panels incorrectly repeat Linear instead of retaining the distinct model-depth labels.

improvement.justification: v6 strengthens the empirical justification through a more competitive embedding comparator, training-setting sensitivity checks, and direct measurements of new-task learning, while clarifying applicability limits. These gains outweigh localized reporting regressions, but their benefit is moderated by missing LoRA details and mislabeled MNIST panels. The hybrid interpretation also needs qualification: Table 11 reports out-of-domain OLMo-Instruct F1 of 42.98 versus 43.57 for matrix completion, contrary to improvement over both components.
